chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'We used to say that it is necessary to begin with the Stone and end with it. But as for today, the people have become numerous.'

key_terms.الْحَجَر: The Stone (referring to the Black Stone in the corner of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: Why did the requirement to touch the Black Stone change during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *al-raf’ wa al-‘afw* (ease and exemption) in ritual practice, noting that the strict obligation to touch or kiss the Black Stone (*Istiftah*) was relaxed due to the crowding of pilgrims. This hadith highlights the dynamic nature of Shia fiqh, where practical circumstances (*‘urf* and *‘azimah*) can modify the application of ritual laws without altering their fundamental spiritual significance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We used to be saying, ‘It is a must that we begin with the (Black) Stone and we end with it. But, as for today, the people have become numerous’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘We would say that we must commence our Tawaf from the Black Stone and end by the Black Stone; however, today the number of people has increased.”’
